numericRepresentationRule.rule: This artifact contains NO JSON number and NO JSON boolean at any leaf, at any depth. Every count, length and cardinality is carried as a canonical ASCII decimal STRING matching ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$. Every two-valued flag is carried as a closed enum string.
numericRepresentationRule.why: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6 law 18 and section 7.4. LB-C2-01 defeated C-2 at v3, v5, v6, v7 and v8 successively, each time inside the repair's own self-certification, because an integer constant compared with == accepts a float spelling of itself and hash(1.0) == hash(1). The instruction 'derive, do not enumerate' applies to the author's own bytes: rather than enumerate the spellings a checker must reject (1.0, True, "1", 01, -0), this artifact makes a JSON number UNEXPRESSIBLE in its own leaf space. A respelling attack needs a numeric position to occupy, and there is none.
numericRepresentationRule.measured: verified by a full recursive leaf walk of these exact bytes; see measuredSelfReport.
numericRepresentationRule.whatThisDoesNotDo: This is a property of THIS FILE, not of the product. Law 18 still binds product admission: a wire value declared as an unsigned integer must be rejected when its JSON type differs, BEFORE any content comparison. See sharedPrimitives.typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob, which states why no test vector in this artifact can enforce law 18.

detail: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 3's EVIDENCE row and IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md note N-3 are literally correct: the identifiers EvidenceBundle, EvaluationEvidence, SubjectSetCommitment and outcomeSetDigest occur ZERO times in evidence.v10.json, as does any spelling of 'merkle'. Confirmed by this author against 62a3a071.

But evidence.v10.canonicalWireGrammar DOES carry a complete EvidenceDigest framing: the DomainEnvelopeV1 record, the SemanticEvidenceV1 field/tag/order table, and commitments.EvidenceDigest. And evaluation-proof.v8.normativePreimageGrammar DOES carry a complete subject-set Merkle framing: SubjectV1, the leaf/internal/odd/empty node rules, the ordering rule and the outer domain frame.
Both sources are CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, which is why note N-3 correctly forbids an implementer from defining any of them and why section 7.1 correctly still owns the recipes.

The one thing genuinely ABSENT from prose, in either document, is the FIELD-VALUE ENCODING RULE for EVIDENCE typed scalars. evidence.v10 declares each SemanticEvidenceV1 field's 'type' (PROJECT-ID-V1, PLAN-ID-V1, RawCasRef<...>, SemanticCommitmentRef<...>) and declares componentFrame = uint8(tag) || uint32be(byteLength) || bytes, but NOWHERE states that the framed bytes are the UTF-8 of the value's canonical TEXTUAL form. An implementer could read 'RawCasRef' and frame the 32 raw digest bytes instead of the 71-byte ASCII 'sha256:<64 hex>'. Recipe R-1 states the rule; the reviewer must confirm the inference. See declaredUnresolvedDependencies.DUD-4.

sharedPrimitives.hash: SHA-256, full width. Truncation is FORBIDDEN in every recipe here.
sharedPrimitives.digestTextForm: sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>, except RunId which is run1:<64 lowercase hexadecimal digits>. Uppercase hexadecimal is not an accepted spelling.

componentFrame.note: identical in evidence.v10.canonicalWireGrammar.scalarEncoding.componentFrame and evaluation-proof.v8.normativePreimageGrammar.scalarEncoding.componentFrame. Both call the same shape componentFrame and blobFrame; they are the same function and this artifact uses one name.

textComponent.rule: NFC-normalized UTF-8, no BOM, non-empty, containing no code point in U+0000..U+001F and not U+007F. A value that is not already NFC is REJECTED; it is not silently normalized.
textComponent.whyRejectRatherThanNormalize: silent normalization is a second place where two different logical inputs become one preimage. Rejecting keeps the input-to-bytes map injective on the accepted domain.

canonicalUnsignedDecimal.rule: ASCII digits. Zero is the single byte 0x30. Otherwise no leading zero. No sign, no separators, no exponent.

typedScalarValueEncoding.rule: THIS IS THE RULE evidence.v10 DOES NOT STATE. Every SemanticEvidenceV1, RunIdentityPreimageV1, TerminalRunV1 and RawProofInventoryItemV1 field whose declared type is an identity or reference type -- PROJECT-ID-V1, PLAN-ID-V1, RUN-ID-V1, RawCasRef<...>, SemanticCommitmentRef<...>, an EP8 commitment, or an RT22 commitment -- is framed as the UTF-8 of that value's CANONICAL TEXTUAL FORM, complete with its scheme prefix. It is NOT the decoded 32 raw digest bytes and it is NOT a re-encoding.
typedScalarValueEncoding.worked: a RawCasRef is the 71 bytes of 'sha256:' followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. A PROJECT-ID-V1 is the 69 bytes of 'prj1-' followed by 64 characters. A PLAN-ID-V1 is the 77 bytes of 'plan1:sha256:' followed by 64 hexadecimal digits.
typedScalarValueEncoding.howThisWasEstablished: by decoding evidence.v10.acceptedGolden.semanticEvidenceHex field by field and observing the framed lengths 0x45=69, 0x4d=77 and 0x47=71, then re-encoding under this rule and reproducing all of semanticEvidenceHex, semanticEvidenceCasRef, evidenceDigestPreimageHex, evidenceDigest, runIdentityRecordHex, runDomainPreimageHex, runId and all six runSubstitutionGoldens byte-exactly.
typedScalarValueEncoding.status: PROPOSED-INFERENCE-REVIEWER-MUST-CONFIRM. It is recovered from a golden, not read from a sentence. A reviewer must decide whether stating it here is adequate or whether the owning surface must state it.
typedScalarValueEncoding.enumOrDeclaredConstantFields: a field declared with an enum is framed as the UTF-8 of the enum member exactly as spelled in the declaring artifact. A field declared const 1 is framed as canonicalUnsignedDecimal of that integer, i.e. the single byte 0x31.

injectivityByInverse.claim: the encoding of every record type in this artifact is INJECTIVE, so two different logical values cannot produce one preimage.
injectivityByInverse.proof: not by inspection and not by enumerating collision cases. A TOTAL DECODER is exhibited: for each record type it reads the record tag, then for each declared field in declared order reads uint8(tag), uint32be(len) and exactly len bytes, and RAISES on a tag mismatch, a length that overruns the buffer, a missing field, or any trailing byte. decode(encode(x)) = x for every x in the accepted domain, so encode has a left inverse, so encode is injective, so H(encode(x)) collides only if SHA-256 does.
injectivityByInverse.whatThisMakesInexpressible: the concatenation ambiguity where ('ab','c') and ('a','bc') share a preimage. It is not a case to be listed and guarded; it has no representation, because each component carries its own explicit length before its bytes and the field boundary set is therefore a function of the byte string alone.
injectivityByInverse.executed: the decoder was run against every record encoded for every test vector in this artifact and the round trip was asserted each time. It is not a claim about a decoder that was never run.
injectivityByInverse.domainOfInjectivity: records, and SETS of records. The set commitment of R-0 is DELIBERATELY not injective on sequences: any permutation of the same record set yields the same digest, which is the point. Under the reject-duplicates rule adopted here, a sequence with a repeat has no image at all, so a multiset cannot be expressed and cannot collide with the set that underlies it. See divergencesFound.DIV-1, because the other source grammar makes the opposite choice.

typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.rule: NO TEST VECTOR IN THIS ARTIFACT CAN ENFORCE LAW 18, AND NONE CLAIMS TO.
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.why: a digest cannot police the JSON type of its input. An implementation that admits schemaVersion 1.0 and coerces it to the integer 1 before encoding produces the CORRECT canonicalUnsignedDecimal byte 0x31 and therefore the CORRECT digest. The vector passes and law 18 has been violated. Only an admission gate placed BEFORE encoding can catch it, which is exactly what section 6 law 18 says: 'Deriving an identity, ref, commitment, or fingerprint from an admission-stage record that has not passed this gate is forbidden.'
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.consequence: these recipes are defined ONLY over records that have already passed exact-type admission. A conforming implementation must reject a boolean, a float or a numeric string where an unsigned integer is declared, and must reject a non-string where text is declared, before it computes anything here. This artifact declares that precondition and does not test it.
typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob.honestly: this is a limitation of the recipe form, not a repair of LB-C2-01. Stating it is the most this artifact can do.

R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.role: THE SINGLE CONSTRUCTION. R-2, R-3 and R-4 are not three recipes; they are three instantiations of this one, differing only in (recordType, domain). Section 7 of the freeze records that every converged repair in this corpus replaced a list of places with a structural property; this is that move applied to the set commitments.
R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.source: evaluation-proof.v8.json#normativePreimageGrammar.commitment (id EVALUATION-PREIMAGE-GRAMMAR-V5), declared sha256 of that subobject 343889cf713931b0e228d84de82cb67d8cb22cc13ae2b3cc71302476f89ef9e0. TRANSCRIBED, NOT INVENTED. Every rule below is restated from that grammar; where this artifact departs from it, divergencesFound says so explicitly.

parameters.recordType: which record grammar the items use
parameters.domain: the closed domain label placed in the outer frame

steps: 1. ADMIT. Every item has already passed exact-type admission (sharedPrimitives.typeAdmissionIsNotTheDigestsJob). An item that has not is not an input.
2. ENCODE. Each item becomes its complete record byte string under its declared recordType.
3. CANONICALISE THE SET. Sort the complete record byte strings, unsigned bytewise lexicographic, ASCENDING. Duplicates: see duplicateRule.

4. LEAF. leafHash(r) = SHA-256( 0x00 || uint64be(byteLength(r)) || r ). Note uint64be here, NOT the uint32be of the component frame. This is the grammar's leafLength rule and getting it wrong is the single easiest way to produce a plausible wrong digest.

5. FOLD. While more than one node remains, pair adjacent nodes left to right: internalHash(l, r) = SHA-256( 0x01 || l || r ), each of l and r being exactly 32 raw bytes. ODD NODE: if a level has an odd count, the FINAL node is PROMOTED UNCHANGED to the next level. It is NOT duplicated and NOT paired with itself.

6. EMPTY SET. If the item set is empty there is no leaf and no fold. root = SHA-256( 0x02 || C(0x30, UTF8(namespace)) ). Note this preimage carries the NAMESPACE and NOT the domain -- see observations.OBS-3, which is a real consequence.
7. OUTER FRAME. preimage = 0x30 || C(0x31, UTF8(namespace)) || C(0x32, ASCII(domain)) || C(0x33, root32bytes). commitment = 'sha256:' || lowerhex(SHA-256(preimage)).

orderingRule.sortedByWhat: THE COMPLETE ITEM RECORD BYTES. Not the logical field values, not the subject text, not any Unicode collation, not insertion order, not producer order.
orderingRule.underWhichComparison: unsigned bytewise lexicographic, ascending. Byte values are compared as integers 0..255. A prefix sorts before any string extending it.
orderingRule.theConsequenceMOSTIMPLEMENTATIONSWILLGET: because every record begins with a fixed record tag and every text field is preceded by uint32be(length), the induced order is LENGTH-MAJOR within a field, THEN content. For single-field records the order over subject strings is: shorter UTF-8 first, and only then bytewise. So 'b' sorts BEFORE 'aa', which is the OPPOSITE of sorting the subject strings. Vectors UC-4 and SS-4 pin both digests so a wrong implementation is identified rather than merely failed.
orderingRule.isOrderDefinedByTheSetOrByInsertion: BY THE SET. Insertion order is not an input and cannot be recovered from the commitment. Vector ED-4 demonstrates this at the inventory layer: the same three items supplied in declared and reversed order yield one identical EvidenceDigest.
orderingRule.whyOrderAtAll: so that the map from a set of records to a byte string is a FUNCTION. Without a total order on records the set has no canonical serialization and two honest producers disagree.

duplicateRule.statement: a repeated exact record byte string is an ERROR. The producer is refused and NO digest is defined for that input.
duplicateRule.why: under the alternative -- silently deduplicate -- the input sequences [a,a,b] and [a,b] map to ONE commitment while the surrounding record can independently declare a cardinality. evaluation-proof.v8's own no-match proof carries subjectCount as a separate field that the Merkle root does not bind (observations.OBS-4). So a producer could declare subjectCount 3 over the subject multiset [a,a,b] and commit to the root of the 2-element set, and the commitment would verify. REJECT makes that input inexpressible rather than detectable.
duplicateRule.THIS IS A DEPARTURE: evaluation-proof.v8's grammar says 'deduplicate exact record bytes, then sort'. evidence.v10's grammar says 'reject duplicates instead of silently deduplicating'. THE TWO SOURCE GRAMMARS OF THIS CLUSTER DISAGREE. This artifact adopts evidence.v10's rule and does NOT claim authority to change evaluation-proof.v8. Vector SS-5 publishes the digest under BOTH rules so the choice is visible and falsifiable. See divergencesFound.DIV-1.

domainSeparation.mechanism: the domain occupies a LENGTH-FRAMED component at a FIXED ordinal of the outer preimage, tagged 0x32, between the namespace and the root.
domainSeparation.propertyRatherThanList: there is no rule of the form 'digest X may appear only at position Y' to enumerate, keep in sync and get wrong. A digest computed under domain D simply IS NOT the digest under domain D-prime: the preimages differ in a length-framed slot, so equality requires a SHA-256 collision. Vector OC-6 pins this by committing one identical record set under 'outcome-set' and under 'universe' and publishing both digests.
domainSeparation.whyLengthFramedAndNotAPrefix: a bare prefix admits a boundary slide: domain 'abc' with payload 'd' and domain 'ab' with payload 'cd' share a byte string. The 4-byte length before the domain makes that impossible. Vector ED-6 pins the same argument for the EVIDENCE envelope.

nodeTypeSeparation.rule: leaf preimages begin 0x00, internal preimages begin 0x01, the empty-set preimage begins 0x02, the outer preimage begins 0x30. All four are distinct at byte 0.
nodeTypeSeparation.consequence: a leaf hash can never be an internal hash and a single-element root can never be an empty-set root, so the classic second-preimage attack that promotes an internal node into a leaf position has no preimage available. This is why PROMOTE UNCHANGED is safe here where a bare unprefixed Merkle would need duplicate-last or a length commitment.
nodeTypeSeparation.andThereforeTheTreeShapeIsDetermined: given the leaf count N the pairing schedule is fixed, and given node-type separation the root determines the ordered leaf list up to SHA-256 collision. Cardinality does not need a separate commitment for injectivity.

R-0-typedComponentMerkleSet.fieldPresence: every declared field occurs exactly once, in the declared order, with no undeclared, omitted, duplicated, reordered, overlong or trailing bytes. The decoder rejects all seven conditions.

R-1-EvidenceDigest.sectionSevenOneRow: EvidenceDigest byte recipe -- a LITERAL row of the section 7.1 table
R-1-EvidenceDigest.domainSeparatorIsDistinct: it is the only identity in this artifact using the DomainEnvelopeV1 framing with this domain. RunId uses opensip.run-id.v1 in the same framing; the three set commitments use a different outer frame entirely (0x30 vs 0x8e at byte 0), so no digest from any other context in this cluster can be valid here.

semanticEvidenceV1.fieldOrderIsExact: the thirteen fields occur once each, in this order. No optional field exists. No undeclared byte is admitted.

fields.name: verdictDerivationCommitment

semanticEvidenceV1.forbiddenFields: evidence.v10 forbids requestId, executionId, attemptId, correlationId, runId, runSealRef, evidenceDigest, every timestamp form, clocks, processId, physicalLocators, objectStates, unitAvailabilityRecords, lease, fence, ledger, lineage, sourceRunId, effectiveCapability and authoritative. Because the record is CLOSED and the decoder rejects any undeclared byte, forbiddenness is enforced by the grammar rather than by a scan.
semanticEvidenceV1.whyEvidenceDigestIsSelfExcluded: evidenceDigest is forbidden INSIDE SemanticEvidenceV1. The digest is computed over the record; a record containing its own digest has no fixed point. This is what makes IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 6's requirement that AttemptMetadata and ExecutionId are excluded by construction meaningful for R-1 law LN-13: two attempts differing only in ExecutionId encode identical SemanticEvidenceV1 bytes, so they produce one identical EvidenceDigest. That is a CONSEQUENCE of the closed field list, not an extra rule.

rawProofInventoryV1.bytes: 0x81 || C(0x88, canonicalUnsignedDecimal(schemaVersion)) || C(0x89, UTF8(projectId)) || C(0x8a, items)
rawProofInventoryV1.items: items = concatenation of C(0x8b, itemRecord) over the SORTED item record byte strings. THE SORT IS OVER THE UNFRAMED ITEM RECORD BYTES AND HAPPENS BEFORE THE 0x8b FRAMING.
rawProofInventoryV1.itemRecord: RawProofInventoryItemV1 = 0x80 || C(0x85, UTF8(recordCasRef)) || C(0x86, UTF8(recordKind)) || C(0x87, UTF8(requiredForCapability))
rawProofInventoryV1.duplicates: REJECT, per R-0.duplicateRule. Two identical item records are an error.
rawProofInventoryV1.zeroItems: encodable. evidence.v10's equalityRule permits zero items only when the retention authority validates that capability; that is an ADMISSION condition, not an encoding condition, and vector ED-3 pins the encoding either way.

whyTwoDifferentLogicalValuesCannotShareA: Every field is C(tag, bytes) with an explicit uint32be length, at a fixed ordinal, with a tag unique within the record. The decoder in sharedPrimitives.injectivityByInverse reconstructs the exact field list from the byte string alone and rejects everything outside the image. encode therefore has a left inverse and is injective.

Adjacent-field sliding is inexpressible: the length precedes the bytes, so no reader can choose a different boundary. Vectors UC-6-A and UC-6-B pin this at the record layer ('a','bc') versus ('ab','c').
The nested inventory cannot bleed into the enclosing record because it is itself length-framed at 0x9a.

The domain cannot slide into the payload because it is length-framed at 0x8c. Vector ED-6 pins this with the near-miss pair ('opensip.semantic-evidence.v1', 'PAYLOAD') and ('opensip.semantic-evidence.v', '1PAYLOAD').

The inventory item ORDER is not an input: items are sorted by record bytes, so producer order cannot vary the digest. Vector ED-4 pins that. Under the adopted REJECT rule a repeated item has no image, so a multiset of proof refs cannot collapse into the set that underlies it.

RESIDUAL, STATED: injectivity is on the RECORD, and the record's field VALUES are typed identities minted elsewhere. If two distinct evaluations could ever produce identical values in all thirteen fields they would share an EvidenceDigest -- correctly, since they are the same evidence. Whether the thirteen fields are SUFFICIENT to distinguish semantically distinct evidence is a contract question about evidence.v10's field set, not an encoding question, and this artifact does not answer it.

relatedButDistinctDigest.semanticEvidenceCasRef: sha256:<lowerhex SHA-256(exact SemanticEvidenceV1 bytes))>, with NO domain envelope.
relatedButDistinctDigest.rule: semanticEvidenceCasRef and EvidenceDigest are computed over the SAME object and are DIFFERENT VALUES. A producer must never substitute one for the other. Vector ED-7 pins both for one input so the substitution is falsifiable.

R-2-universeCommitment.domainSeparator: the ASCII string 'universe' at C(0x32, ...) of the outer frame, under namespace 'opensip.evaluation-proof.v2'.
R-2-universeCommitment.domainSeparatorIsDistinct: distinct from 'subject-set', 'outcome-set' and every other member of the closed domain vocabulary. Vector OC-6 pins a same-root cross-domain pair and the digests differ.

theFourFramingQuestionsANSWEREDEXPLICITL.nodeAndLeafDomainSeparation: leaf preimage begins 0x00 and carries uint64be(recordLength) before the record; internal preimage begins 0x01 and carries exactly two 32-byte hashes; empty-set preimage begins 0x02. Distinct at byte 0, so a leaf hash is never an internal hash and no node can be promoted across types.
theFourFramingQuestionsANSWEREDEXPLICITL.oddNodeRule: PROMOTE THE FINAL NODE UNCHANGED to the next level. It is NOT duplicated and NOT paired with itself. Vectors SS-3 and UC-5 each publish the normative digest AND the counterDigestDuplicateLastRule that a Bitcoin-style duplicate-last implementation would produce, so the two rules are distinguishable by test rather than by reading.
theFourFramingQuestionsANSWEREDEXPLICITL.emptySet: root = SHA-256(0x02 || C(0x30, UTF8('opensip.evaluation-proof.v2'))). The empty root carries the NAMESPACE ONLY and not the domain, so the empty root is IDENTICAL across subject-set, universe and outcome-set. The final COMMITMENTS still differ because the outer frame adds the domain -- vectors SS-1, UC-1 and OC-1 pin three different commitments. An implementation that compares ROOTS rather than COMMITMENTS conflates them. See observations.OBS-3.
theFourFramingQuestionsANSWEREDEXPLICITL.singleElement: root = leafHash(theOneRecord). No fold occurs. The root is a leaf hash, which is why node-type separation is load-bearing rather than decorative. Vectors SS-2, UC-2, UC-3, OC-2, OC-3 are all single-element.
theFourFramingQuestionsANSWEREDEXPLICITL.orderingIsDefinedBy: THE SET, under sorting of the COMPLETE SubjectV1 RECORD BYTES, unsigned bytewise lexicographic ascending. NOT insertion order. NOT the Unicode order of the subject strings. Because C(0x05, ...) places uint32be(length) before the UTF-8, the induced order is LENGTH-MAJOR then bytewise: 'b' sorts before 'aa'. Vector SS-4 publishes the normative digest and the counterDigestNaiveTextSort a subject-string sort would produce.

divergencesFound.rule: Two places where the CORPUS says two things. Neither is resolved here. An authoring agent that silently picked one and moved on would be manufacturing agreement.

DIV-1-DUPLICATE-RULE.severity: AFFECTS EVERY SET COMMITMENT IN THIS CLUSTER

sourceA.verbatim: deduplicate exact record bytes, then sort unsigned bytewise ascending

sourceB.verbatim: sort complete item record bytes unsigned; reject duplicates instead of silently deduplicating

DIV-1-DUPLICATE-RULE.whyItMatters: under deduplicate, the multiset [a,a,b] and the set [a,b] have ONE identical commitment -- measured and published at vector SS-5. evaluation-proof.v8's no-match proof carries subjectCount as an independent field the root does not bind, so a producer can declare a cardinality the commitment cannot contradict.
DIV-1-DUPLICATE-RULE.whyThatChoice: REJECT makes the ambiguous input inexpressible; deduplicate makes it merely undetected. But the choice belongs to the owning surfaces, not to this artifact.
DIV-1-DUPLICATE-RULE.unresolved: YES. This artifact cannot change evaluation-proof.v8, and evidence.v10 imports commitment VALUES from it. If the source grammars are not reconciled, an EVIDENCE-side verifier and an EVALUATION-PROOF-side producer will disagree about whether a given proof is well-formed while agreeing on every digest they both accept.

DIV-2-WHAT-A-SUBJECT-LEAF-IS.severity: CHANGES THE PRIVACY POSTURE OF THE NO-MATCH CONSTRUCTION

sourceA.effect: the leaf carries the subject VALUE as text, e.g. 'src/a.ts'

sourceB.verbatim: A Merkle root over the SORTED list of subject identities, where a subject identity is the content digest of that subject's normalised fact tuple
sourceB.andAlso: The leaves are digests of FACTS, not of source

DIV-2-WHAT-A-SUBJECT-LEAF-IS.whyItMatters: source B was designed so that a no-match commitment retains no source-derived material beyond a fact digest, and it justifies sorting by NON-MEMBERSHIP proofs from adjacent-leaf paths. Source A puts raw path text in the leaf. These are different artifacts with different disclosure consequences, not two spellings of one design.
DIV-2-WHAT-A-SUBJECT-LEAF-IS.whyThatChoice: ONLY because source A is what the live imported vector actually computes: this author reproduced evaluation-proof.v8's pinned sha256:65e3d109be185540e70c61c72cf072243f12cf9a37883b6797a9014255dab1c7 from the literal partition members. That settles what the CURRENT BYTES DO. It settles nothing about what the architecture intends, and evidence.v1 is SUPERSEDED rather than withdrawn on this point.

observations.rule: measured facts that are not recipes and not proposals. Recorded because a reviewer may want them and because hiding a measurement is how section 7.2.2's defect happens.
observations.OBS-1-THE-IMPORTS-ARE-DERIVABLE: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md section 3 says evidence.v10 'imports universeCommitment and outcomeSetCommitment BY EQUALITY from an unapplied evaluation-proof.v8 vector'. Measured: both values are DERIVABLE from that vector's own declared inputs under TCMS-V5 -- see UC-2 and OC-2. They are not opaque constants. This does not make evidence.v10 self-contained; the derivation still runs through an unapplied artifact.
observations.OBS-2-EVIDENCE-V10-IS-INTERNALLY-CONSIST: every identity value evidence.v10 publishes in acceptedGolden was recomputed by this author from declared inputs and matched: rawProofInventoryHex, semanticEvidenceHex, semanticEvidenceCasRef, evidenceDigestPreimageHex, evidenceDigest, runIdentityRecordHex, runDomainPreimageHex, runId, and all six runSubstitutionGoldens expectedRunId values. Fourteen exact byte or digest matches. This is a fact about that document's self-consistency; it is not a review of it and it does not move its disposition.
observations.OBS-3-THE-EMPTY-ROOT-DOES-NOT-CARRY-THE-: the empty-set root SHA-256(0x02 || C(0x30, namespace)) is IDENTICAL for universe, subject-set and outcome-set, because the domain enters only at the outer frame. The final commitments differ -- vectors UC-1, OC-1 and SS-1 are three distinct digests. Consequence: an implementation that compares or stores Merkle ROOTS rather than COMMITMENTS conflates an empty universe with an empty subject set. Not a defect in the grammar; a sharp edge in it.
observations.OBS-4-SUBJECTCOUNT-IS-NOT-BOUND-BY-THE-R: evaluation-proof.v8's no-match proof carries subjectCount alongside subjectSetCommitment. Nothing in TCMS-V5 binds the two. Under the adopted REJECT duplicate rule the leaf count equals the distinct subject count, so a checker COULD compare them, but no artifact requires it. Recorded as an available invariant nobody has claimed.
observations.OBS-5-THE-TWO-TAG-REGISTRIES-ARE-DISJOIN: evidence.v10 uses record tags 0x80..0x84 and 0x8e; evaluation-proof.v8 uses 0x10..0x1b and 0x30, with node prefixes 0x00..0x02. No record tag is shared, so a record from one grammar cannot be decoded as a record of the other. This is a genuine structural property of the pair, and it is an ACCIDENT of independent authorship rather than a stated invariant of either document.
observations.OBS-6-0x30-IS-OVERLOADED-WITHIN-EP8: 0x30 is both the outer-frame record tag and the namespace blob tag inside the empty-set preimage, and it is also PolicyV2's policyRef field tag. The three are unambiguous because they occupy different positions in preimages that differ at byte 0, but the tag registry is not injective and a reader may reasonably expect it to be.

The recipes are transcriptions plus one inferred rule. Where this artifact departs from a source it says so; where a source is silent it says so. It contains no novel cryptographic design and should not be credited with any.
No implementation, no store, no execution path and no product code was written or run. The evidence grade is SPECIFIED / IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED.
